title: Users and groups
subtitle: passwd, shadow, group files, and account tools — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Kernel, files, sudo, and services key off numbers — not the pretty login or group name
cards.notes: Every process runs as a user in one or more groups.

cards.meaning: name : password : UID : GID : comment : home : shell
cards.notes: passwd = who. Expiration is not on this line.

cards.meaning: Login label you type at SSH or su; unique on the box; only a label
cards.notes: Typical: short, lowercase, no spaces. Renaming does not change file ownership.

cards.meaning: Rename the login name; UID and file ownership stay the same
cards.notes: Ownership is stored as UID, not the string name.

cards.meaning: Hash is in /etc/shadow (root-only), not in world-readable passwd
cards.notes: Stops ordinary users from copying hashes out of passwd and cracking them.

cards.meaning: Password login is locked
cards.notes: Empty password field (rare, dangerous) means no password required.

cards.meaning: Integer the kernel uses as “who is this”; every file has an owner UID
cards.notes: Two passwd lines with the same UID are the same identity to the kernel.

cards.meaning: root — unlimited privileges
cards.notes: Do not use root without necessity. Prefer sudo for one command.

cards.meaning: Daemons and system accounts (daemon, bin, nobody) — not humans
cards.notes: Regular people often start at 1000 (sometimes 500 on older Red Hat).

cards.meaning: User’s required primary group number; new files usually get this GID
cards.notes: Extra groups are not this field — they live in /etc/group.

cards.meaning: Free-text description (full name, Super-User); optional for login
cards.notes: finger and some mail tools display it. Extra comma-separated subfields exist; most servers use the first part.

cards.meaning: User’s directory for configs, .ssh, files; login sets $HOME and cds here
cards.notes: Missing/unreadable home may still allow login; shell starts elsewhere and dotfiles are skipped.

cards.meaning: Program started at interactive login ($SHELL)
cards.notes: User can still type bash after they are in. Set with useradd -s / usermod -s.

cards.meaning: Account exists for daemons/files but must not get a login shell
cards.notes: chsh lets a user change their own shell if it is listed in /etc/shells.

cards.meaning: Stored in /etc/shadow (not passwd): aging, warn, inactive, expire
cards.notes: After expiry, login is refused even if the password is correct.

cards.meaning: passwd = who (name, UID, GID, home, shell, comment); shadow = secret and time
cards.notes: x means the secret is next door in shadow.

cards.meaning: All users including system accounts: name, UID, GID, comment, home, shell
cards.notes: World-readable. Hashes are not here when the second field is x.

cards.meaning: Password hash, lock markers, aging, and account expiration (root only)
cards.notes: passwd writes the hash; you never type the hash yourself.

cards.meaning: name : password : GID : user1,user2,...
cards.notes: group line = name + GID + extra people.

cards.meaning: Label for chgrp, usermod -G, ls -l; ownership is stored as GID
cards.notes: groupmod -n renames; existing files still show the new name because the number did not change.

cards.meaning: Old newgrp secret; almost always empty or x; hash (if any) in /etc/gshadow
cards.notes: You almost never set this — access is membership, not a group secret.

cards.meaning: Integer the kernel uses as “which group”
cards.notes: GID 0 is typically the root group. Two names with the same GID are the same group — avoid that.

cards.meaning: Primary = GID in /etc/passwd only; supplementary = name on /etc/group member list
cards.notes: You may not appear in /etc/group for your primary GID.

cards.meaning: Nobody is a supplementary member; users can still have that GID as primary in passwd
cards.notes: Empty list ≠ unused group. Common with useradd private groups.

cards.meaning: Group name, GID, and supplementary member usernames
cards.notes: Primary group of a user is the GID field in /etc/passwd.

cards.meaning: Group password hash if one exists (root-only); rare
cards.notes: Group counterpart of /etc/shadow.

cards.meaning: List users: name:x:UID:GID:comment:home:shell
List groups: name:x:GID:user,user
Show password hashes and expiry (root only)
Print UID, primary GID, and all groups for the process
cards.notes: groups / id merge primary and supplementary sources.

cards.meaning: Print numeric UID
Print primary GID
Print every GID the process has
Group names of the current user
cards.notes: Memory hook: groups = who am I in.

cards.meaning: Group names of alice
Show password aging and account expiry from shadow
Switch user with login shell: their home and profile env; needs their password
cards.notes: su = their password. - = full login (home + profile).

cards.meaning: Switch user but keep most of your environment
cards.notes: Still needs that user’s password (except root switching down).

cards.meaning: Switch to root; asks for root password
cards.notes: su alone is the same as su root.

cards.meaning: Run a program with another user’s privileges (usually root); asks for YOUR password if allowed
cards.notes: sudo = your password via sudoers. su = target password.

cards.meaning: Root shell without knowing root’s password (if sudoers allows)
cards.notes: Root shell via sudoers, not via root’s secret.

cards.meaning: Create a user with home directory and login shell
cards.notes: Needs root. -d home, -s shell.

cards.meaning: Delete the account but leave the home directory
Delete the account and remove home/files
cards.notes: -r = also remove the house.

cards.meaning: Change the user’s home path
Change the login shell
Set account expiration date
Append a supplementary group; without -a, -G replaces the extra-group set
cards.notes: -a = append. Critical: bare -G wipes other extras.

cards.meaning: Change your password (old + new twice); writes the hash in shadow
cards.notes: Root can passwd otheruser without the old password.

cards.meaning: Root sets another user’s password without knowing the old one
Show login name, home directory, and shell
cards.notes: Also can display the GECOS comment.

cards.meaning: Create a group
cards.notes: *add create, *del delete, *mod change.

cards.meaning: Delete a group
Rename a group; GID unchanged
cards.notes: groupmod can also change GID.

cards.meaning: Add user as a supplementary group member
cards.notes: Same idea as usermod -aG.
